searchText: 0? You should try testing it It is still a function of not being included due to slow propagation, however the calculus has changed. Since there is no block reward it is technically a function of reward from fees from the block without your transaction. There is still a proposer reward though, albeit lower (0.03 ETH or something). And timing is a bit different as well, given the 4 second window (and boost scoring). You don't, at least not always, have to worry about being as fast as possible. The risk comes from a combination of not being able to wait as long to see if better transactions (more fees) become available, and of increased risk of a network hiccup delaying your block sufficiently to get excluded. I was curious when that box would be opened ^^ imo arguments about block propagation don't hold quite as much anymore (eg the ones here: https://notes.ethereum.org/@barnabe/rk5ue1WF_). In a PBS world it might matter even less too, as long as it's not zero (builders can price in your PF early). If we lower PF it doesn't mean fees will be cheaper though, but we would have basefee closer to the true market price, which is nice has the planning of the next fork started? https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/745077610685661265/1020003119649787925 https://twitter.com/Butta_eth/status/1570788474487443456 <:sadpepe:360939478749282306> turns out mev boost is not as important as we thought it will be I'd say it is also due to the current conditions. There aren't that many MEV opportunities in a bearish market would be interesting to see these figures when activity picks up again it's been like this for a few months, sure if gas prices go up and eth price is more volitile to cause liquidations Does this show mev though? how does it if mev is paid by a transaction in the block? most mev is paid via transaction fees. so yes can't track backdoor deals obviously 😉 This is incorrect. Most MEV is paid via `block.coinbase.call{value: amount}("")` This is so the bundle only pays if the searcher got paid. Gas fees are *always* paid, so block producers could include the transaction even if it failed and get paid. You need to look at the net change in balance of the block author/builder/coinbase (I forget what we named this field on the block header) to figure out the real amount. how do you prove that this transfer is indeed mev? considering there is very little mev-boost usage right now, i'd say most are done via tx fees 🙂 You could do deep tracing to check if the COINBASE address was referenced, that is a strong indicator. That being said, it is almost always the case that when the block.coinbase gets paid it is because of MEV. Most what? No searcher pays with fees. It is a great way to lose money fast. Sorry, I take that back. Open air gas auctions *do* pay with fees. at that point you can also start figuring out backdoor deals but in post merge world, as per my understanding how mev builders are setup, block's coinbase might not be the validator's fee recipient, but entire builder bid might be paid via a transaction (to validator) So that class of MEV is done with fees, though that is much less common since FB launched. that breaks the correlation Hmm, you are suggesting that the block producer will accept a block with someone else's address as the fee recipient? How do they ensure they get paid? yes thats what the spec says that could happen so we don't have strict fee recipient checks before signing the block for builder builder scoring? right now its trust the builder There isn't even a proof that the new state root contains an updated balance? That just seems unnecessarily trusted. You could trivially provide a proof of new balance along with the block header. no no proof, just a signed builder bid (promised amount) yes that should be easy to include as well as verify 😖 Ugh. It is so easy to provide header + hash + proof of balance change. The only thing that needs to be blinded is the body. It’s against the producer rules to include reverting bundles / transactions unless the bundle sender explicitly asks for it. Hence paying via gas price it the most gas efficient was to pay the proposer. You can pay with coinbase and not need to trust, or you can pay with fees and need to trust. There is no downside to paying with coinbase, so it is unnecessarily risky for a searcher to pay with fees. You always need to trust the proposer that they do not unbundle your transactions You save like 700 gas. It consumes more gas Yeah, ~700 or so. Which is significantly for high competitive mev strategies Eh... it is pretty rare the race comes down to 700 gas, and if you pay with gas reorgs can wreck you without anyone being malicious. Tell this to the bot that has like 14 zeros at the beginning of their contract address to save on gas One time computational cost with no increased risk to them. The risk of reorg (non malicious) is not worth the 700 gas IMO. You protect against reorgs by making your bundle fail in successive blocks so the amount of gas you pay is limited just fyi, from: https://docs.flashbots.net/flashbots-mev-boost/block%20builders Also with pos risk of reorgs is greatly reduced compared to pow i think the balance proof is good enough, its easily verifiable <@301186049323958275> whats is your github id, want to refer in a quick dirty **draft** PR (https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/pull/51) to push discussion on this front i am doing to builder-specs
